scope: Process isolation only; no P3, canonical/parser/PackStore/bibliography/builder/scheduler changes

conditions.initial_state: Each B uses new PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenSearch and PackStore. Each C uses independent cold copies of the same verified P2C B1 database/index and readonly canonical packs.
conditions.timer: B historical enqueue-to-complete-original-verifier retained for comparable table; actual ingest started_at-to-same-verifier separately reported. Both include durable indexing, refresh, all queues drained and all 11032 searchable. Active stages overlap and are not summed.
conditions.resources: CPU percent uses 100% per core. API, ingest and Python remain in the original application benchmark container; isolated projection runs in its own container. Both container envelopes and end-to-end timer windows are retained; process RSS and application reservations are distinct.
conditions.latency_probe: Original authenticated internal HTTP probe, no gateway; 3 warmups then 100 sequential samples per endpoint. Search, detail, reader measured successively. Backlog 5000 current + 5000 regenerated historical views or 5000 text. Per-endpoint drained counts preserved; 30s empty-queue CPU observation.
conditions.instrumentation: Original P0/P1B.1/P2C profilers and verifiers retained; P2D Node CPU/RSS/SQL/pool sampling, event-loop histogram and PostgreSQL activity observer enabled identically in all new B/C profiles. Historical P2C B did not enable these extra diagnostics.

process_roles.api: HTTP, personal jobs and operational monitoring; projection scheduler only in inline mode
process_roles.projection: Same API image; separate Node entrypoint, same existing scheduler and engines; read-only PackStore; internal network, no ports
process_roles.ingest: Unchanged Node/Python pipeline, no ZIP parallelism

conditions.benchmark_quotas: No CPU/RAM limits for any container; same shared host, no concurrent build/benchmark. Additional process has a separate pool (12 connections), heap and event loop; extra resource use is measured, not constrained away.

methodology: Same updated image for all P2D profiles; inline versus isolated B1 changes process role only. B2 also changes existing batch/publish lane settings.
B starts at durable enqueue, also reports actual ingest start; ends only after all works are searchable and all queues empty. Original P0/P1B.1 verifier retained.

C clones the same stopped P2C B1 PostgreSQL and OpenSearch fixture; readonly canonical PackStore. 5000 current+historical jobs or 5000 text jobs; 3 warmups then 100 authenticated sequential requests per endpoint, internal HTTP without gateway.

First text pair inline then isolated; repeat reverses order. No artificial worker throttling. Endpoint queue counts, drained work and external service deltas retained; different drained work prevents exact equal-contention causal claims.

P2D optional diagnostics identical across profiles: per-second Node CPU/RSS/SQL/pool measurements, event-loop 10 ms resolution, PostgreSQL wait-class samples at 1 Hz; OpenSearch client time to response headers. Cumulative SQL time may overlap; per-second query timing observes Promise/callback calls, not COPY stream duration. Original client/server totals remain separately available.

Event-loop median/max of per-second P95 bins is not a global P95. One-second boundary selection and short endpoint windows limit precision. OpenSearch client latency includes network and client scheduling, not pure server execution.

I/O projection first pre-start sample is unavailable in the general envelope; complete I/O comparison uses timer_window_resources where all counters exist. Container resource envelope includes process startup/shutdown; timer_window_resources restricts B samples to actual end-to-end timer. Application reserved bytes are neither RSS nor Docker memory limits.
Fresh B UUIDs/timestamps differ; each full source is compared against the unchanged P2A reference builder on that same database. Post-fault cloned C also compares the saved P2C source digest.

Historical P1B.1 latency is reused from P2C on the same corpus/probes, not a contemporaneous equal-drain experiment. A (thread isolation) and B (remaining historical regression) are assessed separately.

status.interactive_regression: Residual search latency; process isolation improves detail/reader but does not establish P1B.1 parity for all interactive endpoints

recommendation.interactive: isolated B1, batch16 / preparation1 / publication1; existing application budgets unchanged
recommendation.bulk: B2 remains an explicit option, not a new default: this operational pass is slightly slower than isolated B1. No ZIP parallelism or further optimization is justified by these measurements.

bottleneck.end_to_end: Current/historical catalog feeds full-text; both projection stages finish together long after canonical ingest. B2 halves bulk requests without improving the end-to-end wall time in this pass. No evidence of global host CPU saturation or justification for ZIP concurrency.
bottleneck.interactive: Isolated API removes projection CPU and consistently improves detail/reader P95. Search improvement is not reproducible across the B1 text pair: external OpenSearch latency and indexing/refresh/merge work vary with drained load. PostgreSQL sampled waits do not establish blocking as the dominant cause.
bottleneck.scope: No pure causal effect size or statistical significance from one B pass. Historical P1B.1 processes fewer indexed documents during interactive probes; parity is not claimed under unequal contention.
bottleneck.next_diagnostic: Profile concurrent OpenSearch search/indexing and API SQL time under recorded offered load; characterize service capacity before proposing any tuning. No such optimization or P3 was started.
